provenanceAudit.interpretation: Do not call targetPrice absent or analyst-derived; its semantic/source/live coverage is unproven.

B.consequence: priorHigh20 can never qualify as target because it is below entry, let alone >entry*1.01
B.sixtyDayHighWitness: If the breakout reference is also at/above every prior ~60-session high/pivot, then priorHigh60 and all retained-history pivots are <= breakout < entry*1.01. With targetPrice missing/nonqualifying, target is null and the candidate is rejected before RR.
B.tension: A valid B breakout into new-high territory may become more dependent on optional external targetPrice than a breakout below an older overhead resistance.

A.consequence: Historical highs are often above entry and can provide target without targetPrice; dependence is generally less structural but still possible.

conclusions: targetPrice is not a harmless annotation; if present it can rescue a target-null candidate or become the nearest level and compress RR enough to reject.
The same technical price history can therefore change Formal eligibility solely with targetPrice presence/value.
B new-high breakouts are especially exposed because priorHigh20 is structurally unusable as a target and new-high geometry can eliminate priorHigh60/pivots too.
Current Shadow cannot later attribute RR/target-null outcomes to the source level that actually determined target.
This is a provenance/observability risk, not evidence that the current target rule is economically inferior.
falsification: First measure targetPrice field coverage/provenance prospectively; if effectively absent, analyze the rule as a pure historical-resistance target gate rather than inventing external-target semantics.
Compare target-null B new-high breakouts with matched B breakouts having overhead resistance, controlling setup quality, ATR/stop, liquidity, sector/regime, RS and overheat.
If target-null rejects have worse/no-better path quality or materially worse execution/downside, the gate may be protective.
If target-null new-high B setups show stable superior continuation without worse MAE/cost across independent dates/OOS, only then surface a target/admission reformulation candidate.
If targetPrice-present rows differ materially by source/provider/vintage, do not pool them.
Never backfill historical targetPrice from current analyst targets or later-known information.

engineeringBoundary.provenanceCapture: Potential Class A only if existing already-loaded values/levels are serialized to isolated Shadow with zero new source calls and no Formal impact.
